description: Pipeline Monitor (PM, 简称 PM) is the local pipeline-watching GUI for the Yifu pipeline: a FastAPI app (default http://127.0.0.1:8766) over a file-backed serial job queue under YIFU_ANALYSIS_ROOT/_active. Agents enqueue or attach runs here; operators watch progress, ETA and logs in the browser.

rules: Whole-brain production runs must avoid TIFF intermediates: stream Imaris .ims directly with pipeline_modules.preprocessing.ims_to_zarr and pre-create the inputs main.py skips on (ch<signal>.zarr, ch<reg>_downsample/volume.nii.gz, sample_dir/original_shape.json). See pipeline_modules/preprocessing/capability_manifest.json.

Preprocessing/enhancement is OFF by default in production configs (every preprocessing.*.apply=false) so segmentation thresholds operate on raw stored intensities and stay comparable across samples and batches.

Custom multi-step flows that main.py cannot express (e.g. ims->zarr->segmentation->masked ims) are launched as driver scripts and attached to PM via ActiveStore.attach_external, never by hand-editing queue files. Launch method and driver requirements are governed by launch_stability_policy in THIS manifest.
One job runs at a time. To wait for the current run, poll ActiveStore.has_running() or GET /api/jobs; never launch heavy pipelines outside PM while a job is running.

entrypoints.description: Validate a sample directory under the analysis root (S:\Arivis_Analysis) and append a kind=main job to the PM queue. config.json must exist in the sample dir (or pass config_path). The runner picks it up automatically: the GUI polls GET /api/jobs -> runner.maybe_start(), so a queued job starts as soon as nothing else is running and the browser/UI is open (or immediately after a POST /api/jobs).

sample_dir.description: Must be a subdirectory of the analysis root, not the _active/jobs|runs bookkeeping folders

entrypoints.description: Track an already-running custom driver as a PM job. Call this at driver start (see _run_YF2025063002_vessel.py for the reference implementation). PM derives status from the status file's FIRST line: RUNNING ... / ALL DONE / FAILED ... / CANCELLED, with 'Step <n>' parsed for the step display; write the ISO start time on line 2. Re-running attach_external on the same sample_dir updates the existing record instead of duplicating it.

pid.description: Driver process id; PM marks the job failed if the pid dies while the status line still says RUNNING

log_path.description: Driver log file shown in the PM log view

status_path.description: Two-line status file: first line = <STATE> [Step n: description], second line = started_at ISO

job.description: Synced external job record visible in PM

entrypoints.description: List PM jobs with live progress, ETA (from historical step timings) and SampleLayout result listing. REST equivalent: GET http://127.0.0.1:8766/api/jobs (this call also triggers runner.maybe_start(), i.e. opening the PM page starts the next queued job).
True while any job (main or external) is running. Poll this every ~60 s before launching new work; a running EXTERNAL job blocks the serial runner exactly like a main job.

Start Pipeline Monitor (PM). REST API: GET /api/meta, GET /api/jobs (auto-starts queued), POST /api/jobs {sample_dir, config_path}, DELETE /api/jobs/{id}, POST /api/queue/start, POST /api/queue/cancel, POST /api/jobs/{id}/cancel, GET /api/jobs/{id}/log?tail=N.

launch_stability_policy.origin: Incidents 2026-09-18..23 (YF2025063002 vessel batch): whole process trees died to invisible-console input() prompts, invalid std handles (exit 120 fake failures), PID reuse faking 'running', NAS drops, and unidentified external kill waves. Rules below are the distilled fix set.

launch_methods_ranked.why: The most process-lineage-stable place on Windows: the human sees a death immediately and re-runs. For interactive batches hand the operator ONE paste-able command (the queue orchestrator already accepts a sample list); PM stays a read-only progress viewer.

For unattended serial batches. Parent is the Task Scheduler service, so the tree survives console/session cleanup that kills cmd-started children. See _schedule_vessel_queue.py; pair with the watchdog below.
Only for flows main.py natively expresses. Custom multi-step flows are forbidden here; use a driver attached via attach_external.

forbidden: cmd /c start /b or detached-shell spawns from agent tooling: their lineage dies with the tool's cleanup AND adds failure modes at every layer; kill waves on this machine target exactly such chains.

Interactive input() anywhere in an unattended chain: a scheduled task provides an invisible console where isatty() is TRUE and input() blocks forever (cost: one full day once). Pass explicit flags instead, e.g. ims_to_zarr --reg_channel none.

Relying on process exit codes as the verdict: with no valid std handles python exits 120/1 AFTER completing all work, and killed drivers exit with misleading codes. The two-line status file (RUNNING/ALL DONE/FAILED + started_at) is the ONLY verdict.

Writing to inherited sys.__stdout__/__stderr__ or os.dup2 onto missing fds (raises OSError 9, 'lost sys.stderr'): route driver output through an explicitly opened log file; pass that same handle to child processes via subprocess stdout=<log_file>.
Ad-hoc psutil/taskkill sweeps matching by command substring: they kill unrelated trees (self-inflicted once). Kill by exact PID, or by PID + create-time.
Re-running finished samples to 'verify': region analysis has no output-exists skip, so a re-verify costs ~1.5 h/sample. Skip on status file == ALL DONE.
driver_contract: Two-line status file (first line 'RUNNING Step N: ...' / 'ALL DONE' / 'FAILED ...', second line started_at ISO) written at every step transition; PM parses line 1 and the Step N counter.

Marker file after each completed step (output.done), and ADOPT orphaned outputs: if the artifact exists but the marker is missing, the driver was killed between module completion and marker write — modules refuse to overwrite, so adopt and move on instead of failing.
attach_external to PM at start with pid AND pid_created_at (PID reuse fakes liveness otherwise; sync_external_job validates via pid_matches).
Retry loop (up to 4 attempts per step, backoff) + a pass-level retry (3 passes, 5 min apart) around the whole sample list.
wait_for_nas() before each launch: a NAS drop killed a whole pass once.

register a watchdog: scheduled task every 15 min that relaunches the queue when samples remain unfinished and no orchestrator process is alive (_vessel_queue_watchdog.py, task YifuVesselWatchdog). Any kill, whatever its source, is then absorbed within one period at marker-level cost — this is what makes 'never crashes' practically true.

run post-run QC (pipeline_modules.visualization.pipeline_qc) as part of the verify step: 4 hard checks (label magnitude, hemisphere balance, 25um grid, registration correlation) plus human views (normalized registration tri-plane with label contour + hemisphere split line; 5 random raw+mask blocks as 2-channel zarr). verdict overall=FAIL must fail the driver so the queue stops carrying a bad run; outputs land in <sample>/qc/.
reference_implementations: _queue_YF2025063002_vessel.py (serial orchestrator: status-file verdict, ALL DONE skip, NAS preflight, 3-pass retry)

queue_semantics.storage: YIFU_ANALYSIS_ROOT/_active: queue.json (ordered ids), jobs/*.json (records), runs/<job_id>/ (progress.json + stdout log)
queue_semantics.serial: One running job at a time across kinds; next_queued() is only started when nothing is running
queue_semantics.external_block: Jobs with kind=external are never started by the runner itself; they only occupy the running slot while their pid is alive

reference_drivers: _run_YF2025063002_vessel.py (ims -> zarr -> 25um registration nii -> main.py threshold + hemisphere -> L/R stats)
